question:
A 24-year-old woman, gravida 3, para 0020, at 18 weeks estimated gestational age (EGA), presents for
a routine antenatal appointment. Her partner who fathered this pregnancy has an A-positive blood type,
while her blood type is O-negative. She had some light vaginal bleeding 4 weeks ago, and an
ultrasound in the emergency department (ED) showed a strong fetal heartbeat at the time. She was
given an injection, and her bleeding resolved after a few days. She has not had any complications
since that time. Her obstetrical history is notable for an ectopic pregnancy treated “with several different
types of shots,” followed by a miscarriage at 6 weeks EGA which was diagnosed by an ultrasound
showing only a yolk sac without development of a fetal pole. Her miscarriage was treated with “pills
only, no shots.” Today, her vital signs are within normal limits, and a physical exam is unremarkable. A
type and screen show maternal Rh antibodies are present. Which of the following is the most likely
explanation for this finding? Answer Choices: (A) Passive transfer of antibodies from previous blood
transfusion (B) Cross-reactivity with naturally occurring ABO antibodies (C) It is a normal finding
when the parents are RhD-discordant (D) Recent administration of anti-D immune globulin after light
vaginal bleeding (E) Antibody formation after early pregnancy loss (F) Antibody formation after the
ectopic pregnancy (G) Alloimmunization after recent antenatal bleeding (H) Residual antibodies from
previous RhoGAM administration during miscarriage (I) Development of autoimmune anti-D antibodies
(J) False positive result due to recent methotrexate treatment
 A. Cross-reactivity with naturally occurring ABO antibodies
B. False positive result due to recent methotrexate treatment
C. Antibody formation after early pregnancy loss
D. Recent administration of anti-D immune globulin after light vaginal bleeding
E. Antibody formation after the ectopic pregnancy
F. Alloimmunization after recent antenatal bleeding
G. Passive transfer of antibodies from previous blood transfusion
H. Residual antibodies from previous RhoGAM administration during miscarriage
I. Development of autoimmune anti-D antibodies
J. It is a normal finding when the parents are RhD-discordant
